subject: Anchoring ownership, snapshot evidence, and scrub checklist - Redwood Dedicated
messages:
From: Marco Rossi <marco.rossi@novabank.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: Compliance Portal <compliance@novabank.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Evidence for site anchoring and snapshot ownership

Hi David,

Thanks for the call this morning. Novabank legal has requested a short packet that proves: 1) which snapshots are considered 'anchored' to our dedicated cluster, 2) the ownership/retention window for those artifacts, and 3) the step-by-step checklist you would use to scrub tenant artifacts in the event of a termination.

Can you provide a manifest of the anchor snapshots, a declaration we can rely on for procurement, and an operational scrub checklist (we need the level of detail an auditor would expect)? Ideally as attachments + a short note on guarantees/fallbacks.

Marco
Senior Security PM, Novabank
From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: Marco Rossi <marco.rossi@novabank.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence for site anchoring and snapshot ownership

Marco — thanks for the clear ask. I can get you an initial packet today that covers the manifest and a scrub checklist. A few clarifying points so we provide exactly what your auditors will need:

- When you say 'anchored' snapshots: do you mean snapshots persisted beyond our normal retention (i.e., long‑term retention for backup/DR) vs ephemeral caches and model KV snapshots?
- Are you requesting cryptographic evidence (hashes / signed manifests) or is an operational export and timestamps sufficient?

I’ll pull in Ben (ops) and Laura (legal/compliance) to sign off on language for procurement. Expect a draft packet by EOD PT.

Thanks,
David
Head of Dedicated Ops
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Evidence for site anchoring and snapshot ownership

David / Laura — attaching the artifacts I exported from the dedicated cluster for Novabank. Attachments are: redwood-snapshot-manifest-20261101.csv (rows show snapshot_id, tenant_id, creation_ts, retention_policy, is_anchored boolean, storage-path, sha256), anchoring-ownership-declaration.pdf (templated declaration with legal language we usually provide), and takedown-checklist-v1.xlsx (ops steps, role assignments, estimated timelines).

Quick operational notes (included inline in the checklist):
- Anchored snapshots are those flagged with is_anchored=true; they are stored in a tenant-scoped object store bucket with account-level IAM and are not part of the ephemeral model cache.
- By default we keep anchored backups for the contract retention window (settable per-customer). For Novabank the committed retention is 7 years in the US region.
- Scrub steps include: 1) suspend writes to tenant, 2) snapshot export verification, 3) delete anchored objects (object-store DELETE with finalizer), 4) run low-level disk sweep on compute nodes, 5) crypto-sign and store deletion receipts in audit bucket, 6) rotate and invalidate any associated KV caches.
- Estimated timeline for full scrub (anchored + replicas + audit receipts): 72 hours typical, 120 hours worst case if we need cross-region evacuation.

Attachments: [redwood-snapshot-manifest-20261101.csv] [anchoring-ownership-declaration.pdf] [takedown-checklist-v1.xlsx]

Ben
Senior Site Reliability Engineer — Dedicated
From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: Marco Rossi <marco.rossi@novabank.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-19T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Evidence for site anchoring and snapshot ownership

Marco — attaching the packet Ben prepared and our standard declaration. Summary of what we provided: 

- Manifest (CSV): lists 12 anchored snapshots for Novabank (IDs and SHA256), creation timestamps, and storage URIs.
- Declaration (PDF): legal statement that anchored artifacts are stored in a tenant-scoped object store within the dedicated cluster and will be retained per the contract retention window; includes contact points and escalation info.
- Takedown checklist (XLSX): operational runbook for scrub with owner assignments and audit receipt generation.

We also included the following guarantees in plain language for your procurement team:
1) Isolation: Anchored snapshots are not stored on shared ephemeral nodes and are accessible only via tenant-scoped credentials and IAM bindings.
2) Ownership: Novabank owns the snapshot artifacts; Redwood acts as custodian. We can provide signed SHA256 manifests on request for cryptographic verification.
3) Delete proof: After scrub we will provide deletion receipts (signed manifest of removed object IDs, deletion timestamps, and operator IDs) and a short ops report.

Next steps / ask from Novabank: please confirm whether you require signed manifests (we can generate them) and if you want deletion receipts to be deposited in your own S3 endpoint or in our audit-bucket (we can do either). Also let us know whether the 72-hour typical scrub timeline meets your SLA; we can provide an expedited path with staff augmentation for a one‑time fee.

Links/attachments: [redwood-snapshot-manifest-20261101.csv] [anchoring-ownership-declaration.pdf] [takedown-checklist-v1.xlsx]
Doc link: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/runbooks/dedicated-erase-playbook
JIRA ticket: SUP-4321

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you prefer a walkthrough of the checklist.

-David
Head of Dedicated Ops
Redwood Inference
